correctness.rationale: Two explicit complete finite discrete-Morse matchings on 196,226 nonempty independent faces are individually checked for acyclicity using all 1,457,216 oriented Hasse covering incidences. The first matching has one critical vertex, five four-cells, eight five-cells and an exact integer 5×8 boundary of rank two with a unimodular 2×2 minor. Therefore all nonzero Smith invariants are one. The CW model has no other positive-dimensional cells; its five-cell attaching maps into a wedge of four-spheres are fully specified by degrees, so two unit pairs homotopically cancel and leave three \(S^4\) and six \(S^5\) summands. The second matching has seven four-cells, ten five-cells and an integral rank-four matrix with a unit 4×4 minor, reproducing the same result. A separate transfer count verifies the complete face vector. The all-parameter torsion conjecture is not claimed.

value.rationale: The exact categorical cycle-product torsion question in arXiv:2307.12401v1 motivates evaluating an uncovered natural four-color eight-cycle instance: the article handles cycle lengths divisible by three and short lengths, and cites an eight-cycle with only three colors. Here a complete integral homotopy classification and both adjacent sphere multiplicities exclude torsion for a 196,226-face complex where general theory leaves possible Moore components. This is a specific, motivated finite boundary test and a reproducible benchmark for approaches to the open question, without asserting an infinite theorem or relying merely on computational novelty.
